name: Titanium Dioxide (rutile)
metric: E(1%, 1cm) intrinsic, derived from published mass extinction k(λ) via E1% = k(L/g/cm) x 10. Reflects well-dispersed, ~50 nm primary particles in dilute cuvette / Mie-theory measurement.
primary_sources: Egerton & Tooley 2012 IJCS 34:117 — Mie-theory + measurements; 50 nm rutile k(310 nm) ≈ 60-80 L/g/cm
Popov et al. 2005 J Phys D 38:2564 — Mie-theory optimum 62 nm at 310 nm; 122 nm at 400 nm
Cole, Shyr & Ou-Yang 2016 PPP 32:5 — integrating-sphere on rutile petrolatum films; absorption >95%, reflection 4-5%
SCCS/1516/13 §3.1.3 — cosmetic nano-rutile α(310 nm) typically 50-90 L/g/cm
BASF T-Lite SF and Croda Solaveil CT-100 technical bulletins — industrial k_max in 50-90 L/g/cm range

concentration_nonlinearity.model: f(c) = 1 - alpha * tanh(max(0, c - c0) / scale)
concentration_nonlinearity.rationale: Captures aggregation + Mie-saturation + film-thickness density effect at high TiO2 loading. f(0..2%)=1.0, f(10%)=0.56, f(15%)=0.46, f(20%)=0.41, f(25%)=0.38. Lower alpha than ZnO because TiO2 (a) is less dense (4.23 vs 5.61 g/cm^3) so film thinning is milder, and (b) cosmetic TiO2 is invariably better-coated (alumina+silica) so steric stabilisation suppresses aggregation more.
concentration_nonlinearity.source: Fitted to 8 pure-TiO2 + Ti/Zn-blend product labels (Goddess Garden, Babo, Badger, Blue Lizard, California Baby, Beautycounter); cross-checked vs Croda Solaveil 2-3 SPF/% rule and Sunscreen Company TiO2 1.8-2.6 SPF/% benchmark.

particle_size_correction.source: Egerton & Tooley 2012 (Mie computations 20/50/100 nm); Popov et al. 2005 (peak Mie efficiency vs d at 310/400 nm); SCCS/1516/13.

anatase_correction.source: Smijs & Pavel 2011; Hirakawa & Nosaka 2002; Carlotti 2009. Bandgap 3.20 eV vs rutile 3.00 eV. Anatase is rarely used in sunscreens because it produces 5-10x more photocatalytic ROS.

spf_model.formula: SPF = ∫ E_solar(λ) E_ery(λ) dλ / ∫ E_solar(λ) E_ery(λ) 10^(-A(λ)) dλ
spf_model.blend_rule: For TiO2 + ZnO + organics, total absorbance is the sum of individual A(λ); slight overprediction expected in regions where multiple actives all absorb strongly.

validation.formulation: Goddess Garden Kids Mineral Sunscreen Lotion SPF 30
Babo Botanicals Baby Skin Mineral SPF 50
validation.source: Product label; non-nano confirmed on label
Product label; blend used additive Beer-Lambert

validation_summary.notes: Mean error 29%, 4/8 within 30%, all 8 within 50%. The Blue Lizard blend errors (+27 to +50%) suggest the additive Beer-Lambert assumption slightly overcounts UVB absorbance where TiO2 and ZnO both absorb. Pure-TiO2 fits average +10% bias, suggesting the intrinsic peak E1%=600 may be slightly high; an alternative central estimate of 500 brings pure-TiO2 fit to ~10% mean error.

caveats: Old chart peak E1% ≈ 12,500 was OVERSTATED by ~21x (vs ZnO's ~60x overstatement). Both came from the same parametric 'calibrated effective epsilon' meant for visual comparison, not physical mass extinction.

Peak E1%=600 is the dispersed-particle (intrinsic) value at λ_max ~ 310 nm for ~50 nm primary rutile. Real cosmetic films at 15-20% loading show effective k about 40-50% lower due to aggregation + Mie saturation, captured by f(c).
Range across literature: peak E1% 400-800 (k = 40-80 L/g/cm). Central estimate 600 corresponds to the median of Egerton 2012, Popov 2005, SCCS/1516/13, and BASF/Croda datasheets.

Anatase does NOT need a separate atlas entry. Anatase E1%(λ) ≈ rutile × 1.15 in 290-360 nm; ≈ 0 above 388 nm. Anatase is avoided in cosmetics due to 5-10x higher photocatalysis (Hirakawa 2002; Carlotti 2009).
TiO2's UVA edge is SOFT (388-413 nm rutile, 370-388 nm anatase), unlike ZnO's sharp 372 nm Tauc cutoff. Reflects partly indirect-gap character. E1% values 380-410 nm uncertain to ±30%.

TiO2's high refractive index (n ≈ 2.7 vs ZnO 2.0) drives strong visible Mie scattering ('white cast'). This is cosmetic, not optical — it does NOT reduce SPF, but it limits practical loading to ~18-22% in clear sunscreens.
Particle size drives spectrum shape: 50 nm peaks at 310 nm, 100 nm at ~340 nm, 150+ nm shifts to UVA1. Atlas uses 50 nm as default. Non-nano 150 nm grades need g(d) ≈ 0.65 multiplier.
Coating optical effects are minor (<10% on k) but coatings substantially suppress photocatalytic ROS (alumina+silica typical >95%). All cosmetic TiO2 is coated.
Mn-doped rutile (Optisol, Wakefield 2004) is a niche grade with slightly UVA1-shifted spectrum and >90% lower free-radical generation. Not in the main atlas curve.

Validation set is product labels (FDA-required in-vivo testing by manufacturers), not independent peer-reviewed clinical trials. Pure-TiO2 sunscreen literature is thin compared to ZnO. Treat ±20% as a noise floor on individual data points.

Blend-validation (TiO2 + ZnO) uses additive Beer-Lambert; this may overcount UVB absorbance where both materials are strong, consistent with the +27 to +50% positive bias on Blue Lizard predictions. A future refinement could subtract a small overlap correction.

In-vivo target: same as ZnO model. In-vitro PMMA-plate SPF (ISO 24443) may be 15-30% lower for high-density TiO2 emulsions per Hupel et al. 2024 (the effect is smaller for TiO2 than ZnO because TiO2 is less dense).
Spectrum below 290 nm is included only for completeness; solar UVB cuts off at sea level around 290-295 nm.
